stated: Introducing a Digital Bill of Rights to protect everyone’s rights online, including the rights to privacy, free expression, and participation without being subjected to harassment and abuse. Ending the bulk collection of communications data and internet connection records. Introducing a legally binding regulatory framework for all forms of biometric surveillance.

source.quote: Introducing a Digital Bill of Rights to protect everyone’s rights online, including the rights to privacy, free expression, and participation without being subjected to harassment and abuse. Ending the bulk collection of communications data and internet connection records. Introducing a legally binding regulatory framework for all forms of biometric surveillance.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly addresses civil liberties in scope — privacy, free expression, protection from online harassment, ending bulk communications data collection, and a binding biometric surveillance framework — all squarely within O9's legal/civil rights indicators.

Ending bulk collection of communications data and internet connection records removes capabilities currently used for counterterrorism and serious crime investigation under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016, earning a real verdict on national security posture.

Ending bulk collection of communications data, protecting online privacy and free expression, and regulating biometric surveillance directly expand privacy and reduce state surveillance power — the core indicators of personal liberty.

membership_note: O10 is the primary target; O5 captures the security tradeoff with a clear mechanism (bulk data powers are a named intelligence tool under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016). O9 was considered for the harassment/abuse protection element but the policy frames this as a universal right rather than an anti-discrimination measure, so the effect on equal-treatment indicators would be incidental. O15 was considered for online cohesion effects but the mechanism is too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar.
